scenario_name: Customer flags a suspicious transaction after already confirming they all looked fine
judge_summary: The assistant ultimately completed the key tasks: locking the card, clarifying the Amazon charge, and ordering a replacement with standard shipping. Its answers, when on-topic, were specific and actionable, and the tone remained polite and clear. However, it repeatedly pushed a wallet-enrollment prompt despite direct user pushback, indicating weak repair behavior and coherence around the user's changing intent.

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant successfully locked the lost card, investigated and explained the Amazon charge, and ordered a replacement card with confirmed shipping details.

criteria.criterion: The agent looks into the Amazon charge and tells the customer concrete details about it (what it was, the amount, or the date) even though the fraud review step was already finished
criteria.reasoning: After the user insists, the bot calls get_transaction_details and then explains the Amazon charge as “Amazon.com $47.22… Jun 15 at 3:22 PM… Purchase: Kindle Protective Case – Black… Amazon order ID: 113-8472910-5691823,” even though transaction_review_complete was already true.

criteria.criterion: Before locking the lost card, the agent asks whether the customer wants it locked and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: The bot asks “Would you like me to lock your River Visa ending 4821 now?” and the user replies “Yes, please go ahead and lock it,” before the lock_card tool is called.

criteria.criterion: After locking the card, the agent explicitly confirms to the customer that the card is locked before continuing
criteria.reasoning: Following the user’s consent and the lock_card tool, the bot states “Your card has been locked. No further transactions will be authorized.” before moving on.

criteria.criterion: The agent asks whether the customer wants to add the new card to a digital wallet (Apple Pay or Google Pay) before moving on to shipping
criteria.reasoning: Before discussing shipping, the bot repeatedly asks “Would you like to add your new River Visa ending 4821 to Apple Pay or Google Pay so you can use it while the replacement card is on its way?” and only later presents shipping options after the user declines wallets.

criteria.criterion: Before placing the replacement order, the agent asks whether the customer wants to place the order and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: After the user chooses standard shipping, the bot asks “Alright, shall I go ahead and place the order with standard shipping?” and the user answers “Yes, please place the order with standard shipping.” before process_card_replacement is called.

criteria.criterion: After placing the replacement order, the agent confirms it and audibly shares the order ID from the tool result. Judge the spoken value by whether it is recognizably consistent with the returned identifier; accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches. Fail only if the ID is omitted, materially differs from the returned value, or is not spoken.
criteria.reasoning: Following process_card_replacement, the bot says “Your replacement River Visa ending 4821 has been ordered with standard shipping. Your order ID is RPL-2026-001843,” which matches the replacement_order_summary and repeats the same ID again in the next message.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not re-ask which card to replace or why it needs replacing after the customer has already named the River Visa and said it is lost. Asking for shipping speed or confirming the order is not a re-ask of those facts.
criteria.reasoning: After the initial user message stating the River Visa ending 4821 is lost, the bot refers consistently to “your River Visa ending 4821” and never asks again which card to replace or why it needs replacing.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: When it did address the user's requests (card lock, charge details, shipping options, replacement order), the information was clear and specific, but it repeatedly sidestepped explicit questions in favor of pushing digital wallet enrollment.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: The assistant ignored multiple explicit corrections about not wanting to discuss wallets and needing charge details, repeating the same wallet prompt several times before finally addressing the Amazon question.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The bot repeatedly reverted to the outdated wallet-adding flow even after the user shifted topics and explicitly rejected it, showing poor intent tracking despite otherwise consistent card/shipping details.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The wording is polite, clear, and professional throughout, but some repetitiveness in the wallet prompt makes it feel slightly robotic.
